changelog: New spoken-punctuation superscripts and fractions: with Spoken Punctuation on, say 'squared sign' (or 'বর্গ চিহ্ন') while dictating and ² attaches to the previous word ('x squared sign' → 'x²'), 'cubed sign' → ³, and the fractions 'one half sign' ('অর্ধেক চিহ্ন') → ½, 'one quarter sign' → ¼, 'three quarters sign' → ¾ stay spaced ('two one half sign kg' → 'two ½ kg') — for dictating school sums and measurements instead of typing ² ³ ½ ¼ ¾ by hand. A bare 'squared', 'half' or 'বর্গ' still types as a word. Nothing else changed — it never sends a message.
